questions.text: What tradeoff does a network jitter buffer introduce in a real-time audio pipeline?

options.A: Higher sample precision at the cost of a lower Nyquist frequency.
options.B: More tolerance for late or reordered packets at the cost of added latency.
options.C: Better speaker recognition at the cost of fewer enrolled speakers.
options.D: Faster model inference at the cost of lower text-token accuracy.

questions.explanation: Buffering allows packets to be reordered and late arrivals to be absorbed, but waiting before playback adds delay.

questions.text: A voice assistant’s own synthesized speech re-enters its microphone and triggers recognition as if the user were speaking. Which component directly addresses this feedback path?
questions.explanation: Acoustic echo cancellation suppresses the speaker-to-microphone echo path so the assistant’s output is not treated as user input.

questions.text: RingBuffer uses deque(maxlen=4); write extends it and read removes the oldest available items. After write([1,2,3]), write([4,5]), then read(2), what is returned and what remains?
questions.explanation: Extending beyond capacity drops the oldest sample 1, leaving [2,3,4,5]; reading two removes 2 and 3, leaving [4,5].
